subject: Resample sample or observations within samples for model averaging

messages.author: 4c62fdc31c385890
messages.subject: Resample sample or observations within samples for model averaging
parts:
Dear All,

I am running in CDS engine a model averaging but I am not quite sure if for my data is better to select resampling samples or observations within samples. I got three plausible models for male birds distance data (25 transect lines of different lenghts) with strong spatial aggregation, so I applied post-stratification with overlapping strata to calculate a less biased encounter rate variance. However, when using model average my confidence interval and CV are very large in comparison to using samples as the resampling replicates.Most of my transect lines have no bird detections, so resampling samples seems very prone to generate large variation.

This is the first time I am doing model averaging in Distance, so I am not sure on how to select between these two options based on my type of data.

Thanks in advance for any help.

Sergio

messages.author: 4c62fdc31c385890
messages.subject: Re: Resample sample or observations within samples for model averaging
parts:
Well, after no answer I decided not to use bootstrap and calculate with Jeff's functions in RMark model averaged estimates along with variance using Burnham & Anderson (2002) book's equations and tail area CIs as described by Turek & Fletcher (2012). It could be great if these calculations and AIC weights can be implemented in next versions of Distance program as well as bootstrap approximation with variable probabilities depending on the size of transect lines; all my samples were of variable distances (km) and the program was considering equal probabilities for each of those...

Please if anyone have any suggestion I would appreciate that.

Sergio
